extracted.intended_audience: developers and implementers of MathML renderers, editors, browsers, and software that produces or consumes MathML
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing, authoring or validating MathML 3.0 (second edition) for rendering, editing, transfer, and semantic interoperability on the Web. Includes both presentation and content MathML, mixing with host formats, and conformance/testing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Goals of MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable mathematics to be served, received, and processed on the World Wide Web (capture both structure and content of mathematical notation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML is intended to allow math to be handled on the web much as HTML handles text; implementations should focus on interoperability, accurate representation of notation and meaning, and deployment on the Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended readership and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification is primarily for those developing or implementing renderers or editors using MathML, or software that will communicate using MathML as a protocol for input or output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this document as a reference (not a user's guide); tools and implementations should follow the normative clauses for correct behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML Syntax and Grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the MathML syntax and grammar including general considerations, namespaces, children versus arguments, rendering implications, attribute value rules, and collapsing whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers must obey the grammar for presentation and content MathML (see Appendix A), correctly handle namespaces, and apply the specified rules for attribute values and whitespace collapsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-level <math> element usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the <math> element as the MathML top-level with the attributes and semantics defined by the specification; be aware of deprecated attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations and authors should apply the defined attributes, avoid deprecated attributes, and ensure the top-level element conforms to the spec's expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance (MathML Conformance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conformance requirements for documents and implementations (what counts as conforming MathML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the conformance clauses (section 2.3) when validating implementations and documents; conformance affects interoperability and compliance with the Recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined handling of errors in MathML instances and processors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations must follow the spec's error handling behavior (e.g., <merror>, <cerror>) so that malformed or unsupported constructs are managed in a consistent, well-specified manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes for unspecified data
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of attributes to carry unspecified or auxiliary data in MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed attributes for embedding unspecified data rather than ad-hoc mechanisms; this affects portability and processor behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation markup semantics and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation chapter requirements: what presentation elements represent, required arguments, elements with special behaviors, directionality, displaystyle/scriptlevel, linebreaking, and warnings about fine-tuning presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authoring or implementing presentation MathML, follow the semantics of each element, respect directionality and linebreaking rules, and heed warnings about relying on fine-tuning that may not be portable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token elements usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct use of token elements such as <mi> (identifier), <mn> (number), <mo> (operator/fence/separator/accent), <mtext> (text), <mspace/>, <ms> (string literal), <mglyph/> and their shared mathematics-style attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use token elements only for their intended roles and apply the common style attributes; misuse can break rendering and semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: General layout schemata
rubrics_metrics.description: Use layout constructs appropriately (<mrow>, <mfrac>, <msqrt>, <mroot>, <mstyle>, <merror>, <mpadded>, <mphantom>, <mfenced>, <menclose>, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these schemata for structuring presentation expressions; follow required child/argument rules and attribute semantics to ensure correct layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script and limit schemata
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and use of sub/superscripts and related constructs: <msub>, <msup>, <msubsup>, <munder>, <mover>, <munderover>, <mmultiscripts>, <mprescripts/>, <none/>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement correct positioning and semantics for scripts and prescripts, respecting scriptlevel and displaystyle interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular math constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use table/matrix elements: <mtable>, <mtr>, <mlabeledtr>, <mtd>, and alignment markers (<maligngroup/>, <malignmark/>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement table layout and alignment rules as specified for robust matrix/table rendering and alignment across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary math notation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support elementary math constructs such as stacks, long division, grouped rows, carries, and other elementary math elements (<mstack>, <mlongdiv>, <msgroup>, <msrow>, <mscarries>, <mscarry>, <msline/>, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These additions address elementary notations used in many countries; implementations should render these correctly for international/elementary use cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlivening expressions (interactive behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for binding actions to sub-expressions (e.g., <maction>) to enable enlivened/interactive expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When supporting interactive MathML, follow the semantics and constraints for maction to ensure consistent behavior across processors and hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantics and presentation interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how presentation markup relates to semantics and how to express or preserve meaning when using presentation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider content equivalents and annotations to preserve semantics when using presentation markup; implementers should support mechanisms that allow extraction of meaning where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content markup intent and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Intent and structure for content MathML: the purpose of content markup, structure and scope of expressions, strict content MathML, content dictionaries, and core content concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use content MathML to represent mathematical meaning unambiguously, consult content dictionaries for operator semantics, and apply strict content rules where required for semantic interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content MathML elements and constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct use of content elements: <cn> (numbers), <ci> (identifiers), <csymbol>, <cs> (strings), <apply> (function application), <bind>/<bvar> (bindings), <share> (structure sharing), <semantics> (attribution), <cerror>, <cbytes> (encoded bytes), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the defined elements for encoding expression structure and meaning; use structure sharing and attribution per spec to avoid ambiguity and repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content MathML for specific structures and operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of content MathML for container markup, qualifiers, operator classes, non-strict attributes, and specific operator groups (arithmetic, calculus, sets, sequences, statistics, linear algebra, elementary functions, constants, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map mathematical constructs to the appropriate content elements and operator names; consult section 4.4 for operator definitions to ensure consistent semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecated content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness and handling of deprecated content elements such as <declare>, <reln>, <fn>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using deprecated elements in new content and provide migration or transformation strategies where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict Content MathML transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and behavior for transforming to Strict Content MathML (the Strict Content MathML Transformation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or follow the specified transformation to convert non-strict content into strict content forms where required for semantic clarity or interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation framework and semantic annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotation framework for mixing markup: annotation elements/keys, alternate representations, content equivalents, annotation references, and the semantics of <semantics>, <annotation>, and <annotation-xml>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the annotation framework to attach semantic information, alternate encodings, or cross-references; follow the spec for keys and reference semantics to keep meaning aligned across representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining presentation and content markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on including presentation markup in content markup and content markup inside presentation markup, including top-level parallel markup and cross-referenced parallel markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining markup, ensure correct cross-references and parallel structure so that processors can locate corresponding presentation and content fragments reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoking MathML processors and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: How to invoke MathML processors and recognize MathML in XML and HTML contexts, resource types for MathML documents, and names of MathML encodings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host environments and processors should detect MathML per the spec's rules, register proper resource types, and honor encoding names to ensure correct processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring MathML (recommended behaviors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for transferring MathML including basic transfer flavor names and contents, recommended behaviors when transferring, and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow transfer recommendations to preserve semantics and presentation across transports; implement the recommended behaviors for reliability and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining MathML with other formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and examples for mixing MathML with XHTML, non-XML contexts, HTML, linking, and integration with graphical markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the spec's guidance to avoid malformed combinations and to ensure MathML behaves predictably when embedded in various host formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using CSS with MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using CSS with MathML, including the order of processing attributes versus style sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the specified order of processing and interactions between attributes and style sheets to avoid conflicting presentation outcomes; consult 'A MathML for CSS Profile' where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters, entities and font handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of Unicode character data, entity declarations, special characters not in Unicode, mathematical alphanumeric symbols, non-marking characters, anomalous mathematical characters (keyboard characters, pseudo-scripts, combining characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement Unicode-aware character handling, support required entities, and follow the spec's guidance on anomalous and special characters to ensure correct rendering and interchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing MathML (schemas and grammars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parsing guidance and normative grammars: use of MathML as well-formed XML, RelaxNG schema for MathML3 (full MathML, common elements, presentation/strict content grammars), DTD usage, XML Schema usage, and parsing in XHTML/HTML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate against the provided grammars/schemas where appropriate, support the RelaxNG schema and grammar constraints, and follow document validation recommendations for robust parsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media types registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Request and specification of media types for MathML instances: selection of media types for generic MathML, presentation MathML, and content MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the registered/recommended media types for correct identification and transfer of MathML resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary and spacing notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of a simplified and reconsidered Operator Dictionary (Appendix C) including notes on lspace and rspace attributes and operator entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the operator dictionary for canonical operator definitions and spacing behavior; implementers should use it to achieve consistent spacing and operator semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test Suite and Implementation Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive Test Suite is maintained; test results are public and show at least two interoperable implementations for each essential test. Implementers are encouraged to submit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Test Suite to validate implementations; aim to pass essential tests and contribute results to the public Implementation Report to demonstrate interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: W3C Patent Policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification produced under the W3C Patent Policy; individuals with knowledge of patents containing Essential Claims must disclose per the policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with W3C patent disclosure rules when implementing or deploying technologies based on this Recommendation; consult the public list of patent disclosures.
